title: Oral health in breast cancer patients without chemotherapy receiving endocrine therapy and a CDK4/6 inhibitor – a prospective longitudinal observational pilot study
summary:
Most breast cancers grow in a hormone-dependent way. They are therefore often treated with anti-hormonal (endocrine) therapy, which in many patients is later combined with a second medicine, a so-called CDK4/6 inhibitor. Endocrine therapy lowers oestrogen levels or blocks the effect of oestrogen; CDK4/6 inhibitors slow down cell division. Earlier research has shown that falling oestrogen levels – for example during menopause – can affect the gums, the jawbone and saliva production. Inflammation of the oral mucosa has been reported as a side effect of CDK4/6 inhibitors. How these treatments affect oral health over time has hardly been studied so far. This study aims to find out, so that patients can receive better dental support in the future.
A total of 25 women with breast cancer who are not receiving chemotherapy will take part. They will have three dental examinations at the University Medical Center Schleswig-Holstein in Kiel: before the start of endocrine therapy, 8–12 weeks later (before the CDK4/6 inhibitor is started) and 8–12 weeks after the start of the CDK4/6 inhibitor. At each visit (approx. 45–60 minutes), the teeth, gums and oral mucosa are examined, the amount of saliva is measured, a small sample of fluid is taken from the gum margin with paper strips and a 3D scan of the teeth is made. Participants also complete questionnaires on dry mouth, oral complaints, oral care and diet, and receive instructions on oral hygiene. The main outcome is whether the gums bleed more often on examination – a sign of inflammation. The study does not change the cancer treatment, and no X-rays are taken. Elective dental treatment is postponed until after the last visit; acute complaints are treated immediately. Data are stored and analysed in pseudonymised form, i.e. without names.

interventions.name: Observational group: women with HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer not receiving chemotherapy who are scheduled for endocrine therapy (aromatase inhibitor or tamoxifen, with ovarian function suppression if applicable) followed by the addition of a CDK4/6 inhibitor. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-	Histologically confirmed hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer
-	Planned endocrine therapy (aromatase inhibitor or tamoxifen, with ovarian function suppression if applicable) with planned addition of a CDK4/6 inhibitor
-	No prior, ongoing or planned chemotherapy
-	Baseline examination feasible before the start of endocrine therapy
-	At least 10 natural teeth (excluding third molars)
-	Sufficient command of German to understand the informed consent information and questionnaires
-	Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
-	Ongoing or planned chemotherapy, immunotherapy or radiotherapy of the head and neck region
-	History of head and neck radiotherapy or stem cell transplantation
-	Systematic periodontal therapy (subgingival instrumentation) within the last 6 months
-	Systemic antibiotic therapy within the last 3 months
-	Systemic immunosuppression or systemic corticosteroid therapy (> 7 days within the last 3 months)
-	Severe uncontrolled systemic disease; uncontrolled diabetes mellitus (HbA1c > 8.0 %)
-	Known medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ) or active osteonecrosis
-	Acute dental or periodontal treatment need that cannot be deferred until after V3 (e.g. pain, acute infection, periodontal abscess, stage IV periodontitis requiring immediate intervention)
-	Planned start of antiresorptive therapy (bisphosphonates, denosumab) before V3 if dental clearance of infectious foci is required before treatment start
-	Pregnancy or breastfeeding
-	Lack of capacity to consent
